implReport.summary:
I resumed winter-sugar after restart 10 and carried out integrator ruling 1. The trace of playground-park #3 and kitchen-door #3 (with and without A3) found no defect on those two. No digger is held after the entrance opens, release comes at the same allocation pass in both trees, and there is no second unplugging in year one. On those two colonies A3 changes only which workers unplug, and that changes who becomes the second scout and when the herds are found.

An early probe over all 15 hand-overs did find a real defect in A3. Where the nearest free face of the plug is a crack that no walk reaches (suburban-garden #1, #2), the walker stops 3.3 BU short, outside the bite's throat test. The digger then counted fails and was barred for 600 ticks without biting: sg #1 opened at +559 instead of +270.

I fixed it in src/sim/ants/behaviours/nest/dig.ts: a walk to the face point that ends out of bite reach now sends the digger to the old axis point instead of counting against her. The red test (unplugStandReach.test.ts) is green on the fixed tree and red on the old one, and DEVIATIONS D44 is amended.

On the fixed tree I ran a fresh close (close 2): 15 foundings to winter plus the five long runs, with pp #3 and sg #2 going on to year 3 day 16.
- Year one: 13 of 15 viable, every archetype at least 2 of 3, 261 workers at winter, 185.6 C in store. The bar of 14 is missed by one.
- The two misses are pp #3 and kd #3 at 0.89 of their R27 need. They are the same games with and without the fix.
- Long runs: 114 workers at winter 2 (bar 105). R34 at least 1.0 times in 4 of 5, at least 1.5 times in 1 of 5. R22 5 of 5. R27 at winter 2 in 4 of 5 (pp #3 at 0.87).
- Item 7: pp #3 reaches spring 3 with 21 workers and its queen alive, then rations through summer 3. sg #2 reaches spring 3 with 18 workers.

The kitchen-door #3 long run lost in the restart was rerun on the first close's tree. The report docs/design/tasks/winter-sugar-report.md is complete. I deleted the scratch ws-* trees and /home/user/frozen-wintersugar, and kept the closing tree /home/user/frozen-wintersugar2.

findings.title: Closing tree misses the viability bar: 13 of 15, ruling 1 rerun bar is 14
findings.detail: Ruling 1 says that if a defect is found and fixed, the 15 are rerun with a bar of >= 14 of 15 and >= 255 workers, and the task closes on that tree. The fixed tree gives 13 of 15 (playground-park #3 and kitchen-door #3 at 0.89 of R27) and 261 workers. Every archetype is >= 2 of 3. The long runs give 114 workers at winter 2 and R27 >= 1.0x in 4 of 5 (pp #3 at 0.87). AC4 is met through its 'cause reported before any revert' branch: the report says so plainly, and nothing was reverted. This is a missed bar for the integrator to decide on, not a code defect. I found nothing in dig.ts or the tend floor that explains the two failures.

findings.title: The restated-R14 check cannot fail on time for seed 4 (cold throughout)
findings.detail: Both seed-4 cases (4 lay batches and the 2-batch, 4-worker case) report warmFromTicks = -1: the air never reaches forage gate b before the entrance opens (report table A1-A3: 'met / met (cold throughout)'). The test's bound is then Infinity. The only real limit left is that `opened` must happen inside the 7500-tick polling window (afterTicks 7500), which is the old bound the spec asked to replace. This matches the ruling's wording (a cold hand-over's clock has not started), but the 4-worker case is not held to any R14 time. A cheap way to make it meaningful is a secondary assertion, such as open within N ticks of the first tick at gate a, or a hand-over chosen so the clock starts.

findings.title: The implementer's tend-floor tests skip tendFloor's positive path and its wiring
findings.detail: The two tests inject the floor straight into computeTargets and check only the zero cases of tendFloor (needC = 0, surface not workable). None of the following is tested: that tendFloor sums tendKeep over the workable known herds, that it is capped by the tend demand, that undiscovered herds are excluded, or that computeDemand writes core.acc[TEND_FLOOR_KEY]. A regression in any of these would leave the suite green. Covered now by src/sim/colony/allocation/tendFloor.verify.test.ts (8 tests, green).

findings.title: D45's evidence column gives arm T alone's numbers, not the adopted closing tree's
findings.detail: D45 cites 'year one 15 of 15 viable, 255 workers; ... R27 >= 1.0 x 5 of 5'. Those are arm T without A3. The tree the task closed on (A1-A3 fixed + T) gives 13 of 15, 261 workers and R27 at winter 2 in 4 of 5 (report C8). A reader of DEVIATIONS alone would overrate the shipped rule. Add the closing-tree numbers, or a pointer to report C8.
